newsitem.title: USA: Seagram's MCA looking at sale of publisher.
newsitem.headline: Seagram's MCA looking at sale of publisher.

text.p: Seagram Co Ltd's entertainment unit, MCA Inc, is negotiating a sale of its Putnam Berkley Publishing Group to Pearson Plc at a price in the mid-$300 million range.
Sources familiar with the talks said the companies have yet to iron out details and timing.
An MCA spokeswoman declined to comment on a possible deal.
Several financial analysts, said because the publishing unit comprises such a small part of Seagram's business, it might sell if it could get the right price.

Chris Dixon, analyst at PaineWebber Inc, said if cash flow at Putnam was around $30 million a sale should fetch about $360 million. Putnam's cash flow is difficult to determine because in its financial reports Seagram provides figures only for publishing which includes its Spencer Gifts retail stores.
"(Cash from a sale) could be deployed in a variety of ways and clearly to the degree they've decided they can better use those funds, they are going to do so," Dixon said.
He noted the company would have to consider several issues, such as taxes, before deciding whether to go ahead.

In the five months ended June 30, Seagram's reported sales from entertainment and beverages of $5.0 billion. Publishing, which includes its Spencer Gifts retail operation, generated $264 million in sales, or just over 5 percent of the total.

Earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization for the company totaled $518 million in the five months ended June 30, and publishing comprised a mere $7.0 million of the total, according to company reports.
Analysts said Seagram has not focused heavily on Putnam Berkley's growth since acquiring it as part of its purchase of MCA Inc from Matsushita Electric Industrial Co Ltd.

"It's such a small segment of the overall business that it's not an absolutely necessary part of business," said Jeff Logsdon, analyst at Cruttenden Roth. "It can be collaborative part, even though historically MCA did not take advantage of it."

Pearson, a British-based media and entertainment conglomerate, acquired HaperCollins Educational publishing earlier this year from News Corp Ltd for $580 million. Pearson already owns Penguin Group Book Publishers.
